name: Stickleback
description: The stickleback is a small but pugnacious fish with characteristic spines on its back. Despite its small size, it is known for its complex breeding behavior and aggressiveness.
habitat: Sticklebacks are very adaptable and live in lakes, ponds, streams, rivers and even brackish water. They prefer plant-rich shore zones.
diet: Small predator - feeds on zooplankton, insect larvae, small crustaceans and fish spawn
features: Three free-standing spines on the back
Bone plates instead of scales on the sides
Males during spawning season with red throat and blue back
Very large eyes in relation to body
conservation: Not endangered - very common and adaptable species
funFact: Stickleback males are amazing fathers! They build elaborate nests from plant material, attract several females to spawn and then guard the eggs alone. They fan fresh water to them with their fins and defend the nest aggressively against any intruder - even against much larger fish!
